hints.content:
Begin by moving the constant term to the right side of the equation.

 $x^2 - 6x = 16$

We complete the square by taking half of the coefficient of our $x$ term, squaring it, and adding it to both sides of the equation. Since the coefficient of our $x$ term is $-6$, half of it would be $-3$, and squaring it gives us $\blueD{9}$.

 $x^2 - 6x \blueD{ + 9} = 16 \blueD{ + 9}$

We can now rewrite the left side of the equation as a squared term.

 $( x - 3 )^2 = 25$

This is equivalent to

$(x+\blueD{-3})^2=25$
